metadata.title: The Graphs of Quantum Dilogarithm

extraction_notes.note: Labels qexp, qpenta and Glim are each defined twice (intro copies (1.2),(1.3),(1.4) and the formal Lemma 6.1 / Theorem 5.2); the parser resolves them to the intro copies. No \ref uses them.

Equations (1.2), (1.3), (1.4) and (6.5) are restated copies of Lemma 6.1, Theorem 5.2 and Proposition 5.1 and get no node; (1.2),(1.3) remain as text inside DP2. Survey/history paragraphs of the introduction are not extracted.

finalize() matches environment nodes to facts by text, and these equations are character-identical to the skipped intro copies (1.4)/(1.2), so it placed them in the introduction (EP24 orphaned, EP27 under DP2); parent_id was reset to TP3/LP1 after finalize().
Equation (1.6) is named 'the pentagon relation' and is a formal, uncited known identity; typed theorem (external) rather than equation.
Much of the evidence is in figures (complex-coloring plots); observations drawn from figures are remarks/claims with rigor numerical, and the figures themselves are not nodes.
Lemma 6.7 is mostly a definition of Ruijsenaars's G function plus one identity; kept as lemma with the definition nested as its own definition node.
Stated without citation or proof but standard in the literature (e.g. [BT]); marked external 'standard (uncited)' rather than paper results.

metadata.extraction_comment: The paper contains no proofs: known results are recalled and the paper's own relations (Props 6.3, 6.6, Lemma 6.7) are asserted without argument, so they carry rigor semi_formal.

nodes.statement: Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm function psi(z) is originally defined for 0<q<1 using an infinite product expansion , and it is shown that it carries an analytic continuation to the regime |q|=1, where the infinite product no longer converges, but instead an integral expression is found .
conclusions: Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm function psi(z) is originally defined for 0<q<1 using an infinite product expansion , and it is shown that it carries an analytic continuation to the regime |q|=1, where the infinite product no longer converges, but instead an integral expression is found .
nodes.raw_latex: Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm function $\psi(z)$ is originally defined for $0<q<1$ using an infinite product expansion \cite{Fa}, and it is shown that it carries an analytic continuation to the regime $|q|=1$, where the infinite product no longer converges, but instead an integral expression is found \cite{FKa}.
